definitions.explanation: An initial, unrefined version of a plan, proposal, or document that serves as the basis for further discussion and revision. Often the first stage in a formal planning process.

examples.japanese: {素案|そあん}を{作成|さくせい}する。
{委員会|いいんかい}が{新|あら}しい{制度|せいど}の{素案|そあん}を{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: The committee announced a preliminary plan for the new system.

examples.japanese: まず{素案|そあん}をまとめてから、{関係者|かんけいしゃ}の{意見|いけん}を{聞|き}くことにした。
examples.english: We decided to put together a rough draft first, then listen to the opinions of those involved.

notes:
Composed of {素|そ} (plain, raw, unfinished) and {案|あん} (plan, proposal). Frequently used in government, business, and academic contexts where plans go through multiple rounds of review before finalization.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {素案|そあん}を{作成|さくせい}する: to prepare a draft
- {素案|そあん}を{提示|ていじ}する: to present a draft
- {素案|そあん}をまとめる: to compile a preliminary plan
- {素案|そあん}の{段階|だんかい}: at the draft stage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {草案|そうあん}: draft (of a document or law) — slightly more developed than a {素案|そあん}
- {原案|げんあん}: original plan; original draft — the version that formally enters review
- {下書|したが}き: draft; rough copy — more general, often used for personal writing
- {たたき{台|だい}}: starting point for discussion — informal, implies something meant to be revised

REGISTER:
Formal. Common in news reports, government documents, and business meetings.
